To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracts of 12 plants used in traditional Nigerian medicine showed activity against methicillin resistant staphylococcus (MRSA).

the plant extracts of 12 plants used in northern Nigerian traditional medicine for treatment of various infectious disease were evaluated for potential anti-microbial activities against 25 isolates of Methicillin resistant St. aureus (MRSE) using disc diffusion assay and broth dilution.

the crude alcohol extracts obtained form 12 medicinal plants were evaluated for potential antimicrobial activity against 25 isolates of methiclilin resistant Staphyloccus aureus (MRAS) using disc diffusion assay and minimum inhibitory concentration.

the evaluation of the activity of plant extracts used in Northern Nigerian Traditional Medicine against methicillin resistant S. aureus (MR SA).
the identification and evaluation of medicinal plants for their potential use as antibacterial agents.
the search for new antibacterial agents against methicillin resistant staphylococcus (MRSA).

the extracts of the plants studied are active against MRSA, and could be useful for the treatment of infections caused by the pathogen.

the plant extracts are active against MRSA and could be used as an alternative to the conventional antibiotics in the treatment of infections associated with MRSA.
